input.text: The app crashes every time I try to export a project as a PDF. I've tried three different projects and it happens every time.

labeling_rationale: The user is describing a repeatable system failure in an existing feature. Exporting is already supported, but the application crashes when the feature is used.

input.text: My completed tasks keep showing back up as incomplete after I refresh the page. This started happening this morning.

labeling_rationale: An existing task-completion function is behaving incorrectly and losing its state after refresh. The user is reporting broken product behavior rather than asking how to configure it.

input.text: The calendar view is completely blank even though I have tasks due this week. The tasks still show normally in List view.

labeling_rationale: The user has data that should appear in an existing calendar feature, but the feature is failing to display it. The contrast with List view confirms that this is broken functionality rather than missing data.

input.text: Could you add recurring tasks that repeat on the first business day of every month? Right now I have to create these manually.

labeling_rationale: The user explicitly asks for a capability that the product does not currently provide in the desired form. Nothing is malfunctioning; they want the product expanded.

input.text: I'd love a way to save my own project templates. We create the same onboarding project for every new client and rebuilding it each time is tedious.

labeling_rationale: The user wants a new reusable-template capability to improve an existing workflow. The complaint concerns missing functionality, not a system error.

input.text: I was charged twice for my Pro subscription this month. Please refund the duplicate $24 charge.

labeling_rationale: The ticket concerns a duplicate subscription payment and explicitly requests a refund. Both the problem and requested resolution are financial rather than technical.

input.text: I canceled my subscription last week but I was still charged today. Can you check why the renewal went through and reverse it?

labeling_rationale: The user is disputing a subscription renewal charge after cancellation. The requested investigation and reversal directly concern billing.

input.text: How do I connect my Google Calendar so tasks with due dates appear there? I found the integrations page but I'm not sure which permissions I need to enable.

labeling_rationale: The user wants instructions for configuring an existing integration. There is no indication that the integration is broken; they need setup assistance.

input.text: I need to give one teammate permission to edit tasks but not delete projects. What role or permission settings should I use?

labeling_rationale: This is a configuration question about using existing access-control functionality. The user needs guidance choosing the correct permissions rather than requesting a new feature.

input.text: Can someone walk me through importing tasks from a CSV? I have columns for task name, owner, due date, and priority but I'm not sure how they should be mapped.

labeling_rationale: The user is asking how to use an existing CSV import capability and configure field mappings. The request is procedural and technical, with no reported product failure.

input.text: Does the Business plan include unlimited project history, or is there still a retention limit? I couldn't find a clear answer on the pricing page.

labeling_rationale: The user is seeking factual information about what a plan includes. They are not disputing a charge, troubleshooting a feature, or asking for new functionality.

input.text: Do you have a public API, and if so, where can I read the documentation? I'm evaluating whether your app will work with our internal tools.

labeling_rationale: The user is asking whether a product capability exists and where to find information about it. They are evaluating the service rather than requesting implementation help for an already configured integration.

input.text: Undo only lets me step back through my last 5 changes. After that it just stops working and I lose everything before that point. Can this be looked at?

labeling_rationale: A fixed-depth undo history is a common deliberate design tradeoff rather than a defect, so extending it is new capability. A reasonable classifier could argue Bug Report since the user experiences it as failure, which is the boundary this case is designed to test.

input.text: When I duplicate a project, the copy doesn't bring over the file attachments -- only the tasks and descriptions. I need the attachments in the copy too or duplicating is basically useless for how I use it.

labeling_rationale: Duplication intentionally scoped to core content is a plausible product decision, making this a request to expand what gets copied rather than a fix to broken copying. Bug Report is the defensible alternate reading.

input.text: Reminder emails go out exactly at the due time, not before. I need them a day in advance to actually be useful -- right now they just tell me something's already late.

labeling_rationale: The existing at-due-time reminder is a coherent, fully working feature; a configurable lead time is new capability, not restoration of broken behavior. Bug Report is defensible since a reminder arguably implies advance notice by definition.

input.text: Where can I download an invoice for our annual subscription? Accounting needs a copy showing the company name and payment date.

labeling_rationale: The requested object -- an invoice -- is explicitly named in the Billing Issue category definition, which outweighs the how-to phrasing of the request. Technical Support is the defensible alternate reading since the user is asking where to find something in the product.

input.text: I upgraded my plan yesterday but I still don't have access to the advanced reporting features that are supposed to come with it. Did the upgrade not go through, or do I need to do something else to unlock them?

labeling_rationale: The user's core uncertainty is whether their paid plan change actually processed, which is a billing and provisioning question even though the symptom shows up as a feature-access problem. Technical Support is defensible if the fix turns out to be a simple configuration step.

input.text: I need to change who receives our billing emails -- right now they go to our old finance contact who left the company. How do I update that?

labeling_rationale: This is fundamentally a how-do-I-change-a-setting configuration request with no payment dispute or transaction involved, even though the setting concerns billing contacts. Billing Issue is defensible given the subject matter.

An empty ticket carries no actual support request and should be rejected or escalated rather than force-classified into an unrelated category. Copilot's classifier has no abstain path, so this case is expected to expose that gap.

Gibberish input contains no interpretable support request and should be flagged as unclassifiable rather than assigned a confident category. This tests whether Copilot's confidence score drops appropriately or stays falsely high on nonsense.
